name: Silent Pituitary Adenoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of pituitary adenoma with immunohistochemical staining showing absence of hormone hypersecretion
Lack of clinical signs or symptoms of hormone hypersecretion despite tumor presence
MRI evidence of pituitary mass without radiological features of hormone-secreting adenoma
Normal or mildly elevated pituitary hormone levels without clinical syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of pituitary adenoma with absence of clinical hormone hypersecretion and MRI evidence of pituitary mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of functioning adenomas and other sellar masses.

searchTerms: loss of side vision in both eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Headache localized to frontal or retro-orbital region
searchTerms: head pain in forehead or behind eyes

common.symptomName: Hypopituitarism-related symptoms (e.g., secondary adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism)
Mild hyperprolactinemia due to stalk effect
searchTerms: slightly high prolactin from stalk compression
mild hyperprolactinemia due to pituitary stalk effect
low sex drive or irregular periods

occasional.symptomName: Diplopia due to cranial nerve palsy
Nausea and vomiting from increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
weight gain due to low thyroid function
slow metabolism leading to weight gain

rare.symptomName: Pituitary apoplexy presenting with sudden headache and altered consciousness
searchTerms: acute pituitary bleeding with altered consciousness

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve III, IV, or VI palsies causing ophthalmoplegia
searchTerms: double vision due to nerve palsy
low blood sodium from adrenal gland failure
salt imbalance due to adrenal problems

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated pituitary hormone levels without clinical syndrome
Mild hyperprolactinemia due to stalk effect
Low target gland hormones in hypopituitarism (e.g., low cortisol, free T4)
imaging: MRI showing sellar mass with iso- to hypointense signal on T1-weighted images
No radiological evidence of hormone-secreting adenoma
Possible suprasellar extension with optic chiasm compression
other: Histopathology showing adenoma cells with absent or minimal hormone immunoreactivity
Immunohistochemical staining negative for hormone hypersecretion markers

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of clinical hormone hypersecretion syndromes (e.g., acromegaly, Cushing disease)
Diffuse pituitary enlargement without discrete mass
Reversible with treatment of underlying cause

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with visual loss (pituitary apoplexy)
Rapid progression of visual field defects
Signs of acute adrenal insufficiency (hypotension, hyponatremia)
references: Melmed S. Pituitary Tumors. N Engl J Med. 2020;382(10):937-950.
WHO Classification of Tumors of Endocrine Organs, 4th Edition, 2017.
Molitch ME. Diagnosis and Treatment of Pituitary Adenomas: A Review. JAMA. 2017;317(5):516-524.
